parseDate: Strict supported ISO, slash and English month-name formats. Offset-bearing inputs preserve the instant. Offset-free inputs use the host timezone unless options.timezone is supplied. Ambiguous slash dates are month-first. Invalid input returns null, a cloned fallback, or throws when requested. No native-parser fallback.
parseISO: Strict ISO subset: date-only, or T-separated time with optional seconds, 1-3 fractional digits and Z or numeric offset. Date-only is a local calendar date. Invalid dates return null.
addTime: Hours and smaller units are elapsed time. Days and larger units are calendar arithmetic; month/year additions clamp to the last valid day. Explicit timezone calendar operations reject DST gaps/folds. Calendar amounts must be integers.
getDateDiff: date1 minus date2. Elapsed units truncate toward zero. Month differences count calendar month boundaries, quarters truncate that count / 3, and years return month count / 12. These are not full-anniversary differences.
remainingTime: target minus reference, with the same units and truncation as getDateDiff.
convertTimezone: Default: return a new Date with the same instant, validating the zones. preserveTime:true reinterprets source-zone wall fields in the target zone. Use formatDate/formatTimezone to display a zone. Gap/fold reinterpretations throw.
getTimezoneInfo: offset is hours east of UTC. isDST is a seasonal offset heuristic, not authoritative historical daylight-saving metadata; Intl does not expose a DST flag. Use offset for calculations.
getHolidays: Built-in recurring presets: US federal actual dates and UK England/Wales recurring actual dates. No substitute-day policy, historical rule changes, exceptional proclamations, or complete worldwide calendar. Add validated custom rules/dates for your jurisdiction and year.
addHolidayRules: Replaces a country preset with copied rules. Fixed dates use MM-DD; floating rules are functions returning a valid date in the requested year.
isHoliday: Checks configured global holidays, custom holidays, and an optional supplied list. Country presets are applied explicitly through getHolidays or WorkingTimeConfig.holidayConfig.
isWeekend: Uses the complement of configured workingDays; default Saturday/Sunday.
getBusinessDays: Inclusive local calendar-day count, using configured working days and the union of global, custom, and supplied holidays. Reversed ranges return 0.
differenceInBusinessDays: Signed local calendar-day count. Forward ranges exclude the first date and include the last; reversed ranges negate the corresponding ordered interval.
calculateBusinessDaysCustom: Excludes the start date and includes the end date. Global/custom holidays are combined with the supplied holidays. Reversed ranges return 0. workingHours is rejected; use calculateWorkingHours.
calculateBusinessDaysAdvanced: Inclusive calendar days in config.timezone (host timezone by default). Honors workingDays, excludeHolidays and holidayConfig.
calculateWorkingHours: Overlap with half-open [start,end) work intervals. Supports fractional hours, overnight intervals (endHour < startHour), explicit timezone and configured holiday exclusion. The shift belongs to its starting calendar day. DST-ambiguous boundaries throw.
addWorkingHours: Consume nonnegative elapsed working hours, starting at or after the input. Supports partial days, overnight schedules and absent days (all days). Empty/zero-length schedules are rejected. Search is bounded to 100,000 iterations.
isWorkingHours: Start-inclusive, end-exclusive. Overnight shifts belong to their starting weekday.
getNextWorkingHour: During a working interval, consume one working hour. Outside it, return the next interval opening.
getFiscalPeriodAdvanced: Fiscal years are named by starting calendar year. startDay is restricted to 1-28 so every quarter has an unambiguous anchor. End includes the final millisecond of the quarter.
generatePayrollPeriods: Calendar-year periods; final end is clipped to year end and includes the final millisecond. Pay date remains the scheduled date even when the period is clipped. No jurisdiction-specific payroll policy.
getPayPeriods: Anchored at startDate. Semi-monthly uses the anchor then the next 15th/1st; monthly additions clamp month ends. Invalid frequencies throw.
calculateOvertime: Returns pay factors assuming hourly rate 1. Explicit thresholds are arithmetic inputs, not jurisdiction-specific payroll rules.
generateRecurringDates: Includes the supplied start when inside the end bound, even if it does not match a filter. maxOccurrences:0 returns []. Positive integer intervals; finite bounded counts. Custom searches throw after eight years without a match. Month/year recurrences retain the original day anchor after clamping. Weekend/custom intervals count matching occurrences. Weekend generation rejects an all-working-days calendar. Interval is limited to 10,000.
parseNaturalLanguage: Supported English expressions only; options.baseDate and timezone determine relative calculations. Next/last weekday preserves clock time; today/tomorrow/yesterday resolve local midnight. Strict mode throws on unsupported expressions.
compareDetailed: Absolute calendar decomposition: clamped years, then clamped months, calendar days, then elapsed sub-day remainder. Direction is reported separately.
calculateAdvancedDuration: Absolute calendar decomposition. Supported display units: year, month, day, hour, minute, second. Default precision 2. Omitted larger components are not converted into smaller units.
humanizeDuration: Elapsed approximation: 365-day years and 30-day months. Honors unit filtering and precision. Negative values append ago; month abbreviation is mo.
formatDuration: Elapsed approximation: 365-day years and 30-day months. Negative values retain a minus sign. maxUnits must be a positive integer.
formatISO: UTC ISO output. includeTimezone:false removes the Z marker; remaining fields still represent UTC.
formatCustom: Single-pass token substitution with [literal text] escaping. Supported tokens are listed by getConfigs().formatTokens; d (weekday number) is also supported. Uses host local fields.
formatDate: The eight DateFormat patterns only. Displays an instant in the explicit or globally effective timezone. Strings are parsed first; configureTimezone does not change parsing of offset-free strings.
fromTimestamp: Unix milliseconds by default. Pass inSeconds:true for Unix seconds. No magnitude guessing.
toUTC: Returns a clone of the same instant; Date does not carry a timezone.
utcNow: Returns the current instant. Format with timezone UTC to display UTC calendar fields.
getWeekOfYear: ISO 8601 week number, Monday start and first week containing January 4. Does not return the ISO week-year.
getISOWeek: ISO 8601 week number, Monday start and first week containing January 4. Does not return the ISO week-year.
getWeekBoundaries: Monday start by default; weekStartsOn can be 0-6. startOf/endOf/isSameWeek use Sunday start.
sortDates: Returns new Dates, filters invalid entries, and rejects unknown sort orders.
removeDuplicateDates: Filters invalid entries and keeps the first original instant at each requested calendar precision.
listTimezones: Returns a copy of the bundled catalog, not a promise of every identifier supported by the runtime.
getTimezonesByOffset: Filters the bundled catalog by its static reference offset; use getTimezoneInfo for a date-specific offset.
getConfigs: Returns available format values, actual loaded holiday rule presets, timezone/locale catalogs and current business configuration. Large catalogs are loaded only when this API is imported.
generateBusinessCalendar: Generate local calendar days, or midnight instants in config.timezone. workingHours is the nominal shift duration, not elapsed DST duration. Event date ranges include both calendar days; pre-expand recurring events. Event-specific timezone/recurring options are rejected rather than ignored.
